question: Show that the vectors $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}, 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}, 3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$ are coplanar. [4 marks]
solutionSteps: Vectors are coplanar if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}] = 0$.
Since the scalar triple product is zero, the vectors are coplanar.

question: Prove that $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = \vec{b} \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})$. [3 marks]
solutionSteps: Scalar triple product is invariant under cyclic permutation.
This can be shown using the properties of determinants (interchanging two rows twice).

question: Find the scalar triple product $[\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}]$ for $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \vec{c} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$. [2 marks]
Show that the vectors $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}, 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}, 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar. [4 marks]
If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are coplanar, show that $[\vec{a}+\vec{b}, \vec{b}+\vec{c}, \vec{c}+\vec{a}] = 0$. [4 marks]
